subject: Urgent: ACME reserved throughput falling short during peak — request for burst authorization and exec attention
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@acme.com>

Cc: ACME Support <support@acme.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency & 5xx spike on reserved capacity this morning

Evelyn —

We started seeing a sharp increase in error rates and tail latency on our Redwood reserved pool around 10:03 UTC. Our production models are hitting 5xx errors and token latencies are spiking to >2s per token. We have an active reservation (contract HS-ACME-4591) and this is directly impacting checkout flows for a handful of customers.

We pulled sample traces (attached) — errors are mostly 502/503 from the inference node and queueing time is high. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity exhaustion issue on your side? We need immediate mitigation: either burst capacity for the next 4 hours or a rapid rollback to the previous model variant.

This is priority P0 for ACME. Please advise next steps and timing; if we can get a temporary headroom increase that would prevent customer impact while you investigate, that would be ideal.

Anna Keller
Director, ML Platform
ACME Inc.

Attachment: acme-error-sample.txt (textified logs, 12 KB)

Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike on reserved capacity this morning

Anna — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I’m escalating internally to get immediate mitigation and a brief cause assessment. Summary of what I see so far from our side:

- Your reservation is active and we’re seeing sustained queue depth on the dedicated GPU pool serving your tenant.
- There are signs of cache churn (large prefix variance) which increases per-request GPU memory pressure and causes scheduler backpressure.

What I’m asking for now:
1) Immediate temporary burst authorization to 2x reserved throughput for up to 6 hours while we triage.
2) A short-term routing change to a quantized fallback model variant (compatible with your quality constraints) to reduce memory usage and errors.
3) A follow-up call in 30 minutes to align on credits and next steps.

Jonas / Marissa — can you confirm ETA for routing change and whether we can approve burst headroom today? Marcus — please stand by for potential customer credit decision if this becomes a sustained degradation.

I’ll update ACME in parallel once I have confirmation.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Latency & 5xx spike on reserved capacity this morning

Jonas / team — we see this noise in the US-west dedicated GPU pool. Quick triage notes (observability snapshots attached):

- Symptom: sustained queue depth + GPU memory fragmentation due to large prefix churn from a small percentage of high-cost requests (long documents + long-history chat sessions). This causes scheduler thrash and intermittent 502/503 responses.
- Short-term mitigations we can execute within ~20 minutes:
  * Route ACME to quantized_ggml_v2 fallback pool (reduces memory per session by ~40%).
  * Enable prefix warmup + KV cache pinning for their top 20 routes to reduce cache churn.
  * Apply a soft token/QPS cap on non-critical routes to prioritize customer-visible routes.

- Burst authorization: we can flip a per-tenant override to allow 2x throughput for up to 6 hours, but it requires manual approval from Capacity for billing/placement allowances. If Marcus or Jonas greenlight this, operations will action immediately and confirm once placed.

I’m attaching the runbook we’ll follow for diagnosis + rollback. Post triage, we’ll open an action item list for longer-term remediation (model sizing guidance, reservation tuning, and KV cache QoS).

Attachment: observability-runbook.pdf

Marissa Cole
Staff SRE, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
